# CXNM - Standard - WIN - D - AI Tooling

Blocks GitHub Copilot on personal accounts in Visual Studio; the business licence keeps working.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | Windows |
| Scope | Device (D) — assign to device groups |
| Type | Settings Catalog |
| Assignment | All Devices |
| Source | ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.10 and A.8.1 — setting from IntuneAdmin's Visual Studio benchmark |
| File | [`Baseline_WIN_D_AI_Tooling.json`](Baseline_WIN_D_AI_Tooling.json) |

> Intended for an AI policy that allows GitHub Copilot only for software development and only through the organisation's licence. Without this setting a developer can link their personal account, and company code then leaves the approved route without anyone noticing.

## Standards

| Framework | Controls |
|---|---|
| ISO/IEC 27001:2022 | A.5.10 Acceptable use of information and other associated assets<br>A.8.1 User endpoint devices<br>A.8.12 Data leakage prevention |

What this means per standard and what is needed organisationally alongside it: [COMPLIANCE.en.md](../../../docs/COMPLIANCE.en.md).
